messages:
Samir Patel: FYI - after the midnight rollout the telemetry-collector pods show a big CPU regression. p99 CPU per pod jumped from ~12% to ~68% and p99 span export latency increased a bit. Rolling back helped but want root cause before next rollout.
Laura Chen: :eyes: do you have flamegraphs or a correlating deploy id?
Samir Patel: infra-bot shows deploy telemetry/collector v2024.11.3 at 23:47 UTC. Attached quick flame (link: https://s3.redwood/diag/170912-flame.svg) - main hotspot is in attribute enrichment / span attribute iterator, lots of allocations.
Chris Gómez: That rollout enabled route-level attribute enrichment for routing policies, right? We added per-span evaluation to attach "route_affinity" and "customer_tier" tags.
Samir Patel: Exactly. The change path: when span arrives we run enrichAttributes(span) -> iterate tags + eval routing rules -> append attributes. CPU cost is small per span but we saw a 7x increase in span volume from some burst traffic, so allocations blow up.
Mika O'Neill: Could be allocation churn from building new maps/slices for attributes per span. Any profile showing GC pressure?
Samir Patel: Heap allocs spiked, GC cycles ~3x. Flame shows functions: enrichAttributes::evaluateRouting, protobuf.Marshal for attributes, and json.Encode for console logs.
Laura Chen: Did we switch any exporter encoding? We recently toggled on structured-attribute exports to OTLP proto instead of OTLP-json for telemetry-exporter to satisfy Dashboard schema.
Chris Gómez: If exporter changed to protobuf, marshal cost per attribute is higher but should be less alloc-heavy than json. The profiler pointing to Marshal makes me think we're constructing temporary proto.Attribute messages for every attribute.
Samir Patel: Here's a minimal repro I ran: 
```
for i := 0; i < 100000; i++ {
  s := newSpan()
  enrichAttributes(s) // routing rules + add 3-8 attrs
  exporter.Export(s)
}
```
Flame trace: allocations are dominated by attribute list append and a map copy in enrichAttributes.
Mika O'Neill: Two potential mitigations: 1) Move routing evaluation to sampling decision earlier so we only enrich spans we plan to export (ingest sampling). 2) Use a pooled proto message / reuse attribute slice via sync.Pool.
Laura Chen: Also check whether enrichment is done under the hot path for every incoming trace or only after sampling. We intended to enrich only for exported spans but config drift might have enabled it upstream.
Samir Patel: Current config: sampling decision happens after enrichment (legacy). The rollout toggled the new routing rules but kept legacy ordering. So we do all enrichment pre-sampling.
Chris Gómez: Oof. That explains proportional CPU to incoming QPS. Quickfix: flip ordering (sampling before enrichment) or add fast-path guard: if sampling probability < threshold && not high_priority_customer return early.
Mika O'Neill: We should also limit max attributes per span for telemetry (drop non-essential) and add backpressure: when exporter queue > X, skip enrichment.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rollback of telemetry/collector to v2024.11.2 initiated by @laura at 00:14 UTC.
Samir Patel: Rollback reduced CPU back to baseline within 3 minutes. But we need a robust change: propose follow-ups below.
Laura Chen: Proposed action items: 1) Temporarily flip to sampling-before-enrichment (config flag) and ship as a patch to canary. 2) Implement sync.Pool for attribute slices/proto messages (Chris/Mika). 3) Add metric telemetry.attribute_enrichment_time and gauge for attribute_alloc_bytes. 4) Add an automated test to simulate burst QPS and assert CPU < 2x baseline.
Chris Gómez: I'll take the pooling change. Plan: allocate pool of []*pb.Attribute and reuse slices, plus reset function. Need to be careful with concurrency and span lifetimes.
Mika O'Neill: I'll wire the new metrics + add an exporter-queue guard to short-circuit enrichment when queue depth > 500. We'll also add a feature flag rollout for sampling-order change.
Samir Patel: I'll own the canary config flip and run load tests. Also will add a short doc in the ops runbook: "attribute enrichment cost" and include the flamegraph and mitigation steps.
Laura Chen: Timeline? Can we have a canary patch + metrics in next 6 hours?
Samir Patel: Yes - canary patch for sampling-order in ~2 hours, pooling PR in 4 hours, metrics + guard in 6. We'll monitor p99 CPU and collector_export_latency in Datadog.
Chris Gómez: Note: long-term we should evaluate moving routing evaluation to a separate lightweight decision service (stateless) that returns routing tags only for accepted spans, to avoid per-span proto work on the hot path.
Mika O'Neill: Agreed. Add an engineering spike to evaluate that next sprint.
Samir Patel: Thanks all. I'll post updates in this thread as patches land. :thumbsup:
Laura Chen: :rocket: keep the canary tight and abort on >1.5x CPU or >10% increase in p99 export latency.
Samir Patel: Ack.
